utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-A, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina and Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to begin by ensuring that the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Gotovina, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT GOTOVINA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gotovina. You may be seated. Mr. Markac, can you hear the proceedings and understand -- in a language?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Counsel for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Equipment is working well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Brady. Counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I can hear you perfectly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Could you introduce yourself for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: On behalf of Mr. Markac Defence, Goran Mikulicic, accompanied by my learned colleague Mr. Tomislav Kuzmanovic and our Case Manager Vlado Rendulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Mikulicic. Thank you, all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I neglected to introduce the rest of the team for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: By all means, please do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies. To my right is Luka Misetic and next to him is Guenael Mettraux. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Ms. Brady.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I also should introduce the rest of my team. With me today is Ms. Laurel Baig and our Case Manager Ms. Lourdes Galicia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Brady. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a notice of appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two prime purposes. First, it allows the appellant an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. In the present case, the notices of appeal were filed on 16 May 2011. Thus, this Status Conference is taking place after the expiration of the 120-day period specified in Rule 65 bis (B). The Status Conference was postponed until today at the request of the parties in view of the case's briefing schedule. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by the amended Scheduling Order issued on 1 September 2011. I would like to begin this Status Conference by inquiring into Mr. Gotovina's and Mr. Markac's health. If you wish, Mr. Gotovina, or Mr. Markac, we can have this discussion in closed session. It's up to you. Could you indicate your preference.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT GOTOVINA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, thank you. It is all right as it is. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Markac, are you comfortable with an open court today?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Markac. We will proceed accordingly. I will say something about the recent procedural history of this case. So let me turn to the update of the case. The briefing has recently concluded with the filing of the reply briefs by Mr. Gotovina and Mr. Markac on 27 September 2011. Currently, there are two pending motions. On 7 September 2011, counsel for Mr. Gotovina filed a renewed application for an order pursuant to Rule 54 bis directing the government of the Republic of Serbia to produce documents. The motion will be decided in due course. I further note that on 12th September 2011, the Prosecution filed a motion to strike Gotovina's abandoned grounds of appeal. This motion also will be decided in due course. At this point I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. So for the Defence? The counsel of Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. The counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no questions to raise up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Just two issues to raise, or really they're just points that I wanted to mention. I have spoken to Mr. Misetic about this matter. The Defence has filed public redacted appeal briefs on the 2nd of August. We've written to the Defence, we've highlighted a few matters that we believe should be redacted so as not to reveal confidential information. We -- we're still in discussion about that. We're endeavoring at the moment to uplift the confidentiality of a couple of Appeals Chamber decisions in other cases which I think will be of assistance to the Defence in this regard. I'm confident we can resolve the matter, but if not there may need to be a motion filed either by ourselves or by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I understand that so far the Defence has not answered you definitively.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: I think we have a different position on what should be redacted on the basis of it being confidential. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let's hope that the Defence and you can agree on that. Of course, if there is disagreement parties are always entitled to file a motion with the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Yes. And, Your Honours, just another point on the Defence replies, which we received yesterday, we will just need a little bit more time to review them and to consider our position about whether or not we need to do anything further in relation to the replies. And I've also foreshadowed with Mr. Misetic that we think that there may be a word -- a problem with the word limit on the Gotovina reply brief. It seems on our count to be somewhat over when consideration is taken of the annexes. And we are considering that -- we are considering whether or not to file a motion for clarification of that word count in their brief. And, again, if we do bring this, it will be filed later today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Brady. If it is a matter -- if there is a problem, you know the procedure. You will submit a motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, all. Since there appear to be no other matters to be raised, I would thank the parties for their attendance, and the lawyers, and the Prosecution. I call the proceedings to a close. The Court will rise.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
